header: The reading check: two independent readings of one page (the OCR pipeline's and a second reader's) compared on what matters most, the numbers. Two readers that fail in different ways seldom make the same mistake, so I treat a number both have as confirmed, and a number only one has as a reason to look at the page. The check also catches two failures a score never shows: letters from a script that does not belong in the text (a model wrote Cyrillic "М" and "И" inside a Latin name), and a second reading that stopped early (a model that began repeating blank table rows and never reached the end of the page, or a reply cut off at the length limit).
Pure functions, no database and no model: the callers decide what is stored and shown.

members.name: onlyFirst
doc: important numbers only the first (pipeline) reading has: not confirmed by the second

members.name: onlySecond
doc: important numbers only the second reading has: the first may have missed them (or the second invented them)

members.name: minorOnlyFirst
doc: small plain numbers (under 4 digits, no separator) that only one reading has: I count them, but they do not raise the status, since they are mostly page furniture and junk from garbled lines

members.name: handwritten
doc: numbers inside [handwritten: ...] in the readings (only a model can read them): they can CONFIRM a number of the other reading, but I never flag them on their own

members.name: secondProblem
doc: why the second reading cannot be fully used, if so

symbols.name: asciiDigits
doc: Writes the Devanagari and Bengali digits as the digits 0-9.

symbols.name: dashesBetweenDigits
doc: I treat a dash between digits, written as an en dash, an em dash, a minus sign or a spaced hyphen, as the same separator as a plain hyphen: "(2026 - 2027)" and "(2026\u20132027)" are "(2026-2027)".

symbols.name: numbersOf
symbols.sig: export function numbersOf(text: string, withHandwritten = false): Set<string>
doc: Gives the numbers of a text, each in one canonical form: no thousands commas, and the separators of dates, times and references all written as ".", so 20-08-2026, 20.08.2026 and 20/08/2026 are one number. I do not count a lone digit (list numbers, "(i)") as a number worth comparing.

symbols.name: withoutNoise
symbols.sig: function withoutNoise(text: string, keepHandwritten = false): string
doc: Returns the text without what is not part of the page: the pipeline's own "col11:" labels and the [handwritten: ...] spans.

symbols.name: isMajor
doc: An important number is one with four digits or more, or one with a separator (a date, an amount with decimals, a phone or reference number).

symbols.name: numberContext
symbols.sig: export function numberContext(text: string, canon: string, radius = 36): string | null
doc: Gives the words around the first place where a number (in its canonical form) stands in a text, so a human can judge it. null if it is not there.

symbols.name: oddScriptsIn
symbols.sig: export function oddScriptsIn(text: string, reader: "first" | "second"): OddScript[]
doc: Finds letters from a script that does not belong in these circulars (Latin, Devanagari and Bengali do), with where they stand.

symbols.name: MIN_LENGTH_SHARE
doc: I cannot compare a second reading shorter than this share of the first in any useful way.

symbols.name: checkReadings
symbols.sig: export function checkReadings(first: string, second: string): PageCheck

behaviours: important: 4 digits, or a separator
the words around a number are shown
a date written another way is found
a number in Devanagari digits is found
a number that is not there gives null
the context is short and on one line
Cyrillic letters inside a Latin name are found, with where
Greek and Arabic are found too
a number that differs in one digit is flagged both ways
the numbers both have are confirmed
a small plain number that only one reading has is counted but does not raise the status
a handwritten number in the second reading CONFIRMS the same number in the first
a handwritten number only the second reading has is never flagged
a letter from a wrong script raises the status even when every number agrees
a second reading that stopped early: partial; what the first has beyond it is NOT held against it
a stopped second reading with a new important number is still a difference
six blank table rows in a row are a loop; the first stays, the rest goes, the marker is written
six identical text lines are a loop too
REAL gate pass: the pin code 713203 that the pipeline read as 13203 is caught
REAL gate pass: a telephone number read differently is caught
REAL Hindi mediclaim: the deadline the pipeline read as 20-0802 and the circular number it lost are caught
REAL Hindi gift card: the amount the pipeline read as 215,000 is caught
REAL wage notice: the three daily wages and the totals are confirmed by both readers
REAL wage notice: only a stray 9022 (next to a stamp) is unconfirmed
REAL wage notice, a weaker model's reading: the Cyrillic letters in a name are found
REAL Hindi GPAIS, a weaker model's reading: it stopped early (154 blank rows), so the check is PARTIAL, not a disagreement
REAL Hindi GPAIS, a weaker model's reading: the table numbers it did read are all confirmed
REAL Hindi GPAIS: the cut text is short, not 176 lines
a ${name} between digits reads as a plain hyphen
REAL upload: the same page read with different dashes now AGREES (it was 'differences': only 2026.2027 against 2026 and 2027)
a short year (2026-27) is still a different number from 2026-2027 (that is a real difference, not typography)
a dash that is not between digits is left alone
a real dash between two different numbers is still seen as a difference when only one reader has it
numberContext finds a number across the dash forms too
